Multi-Arduino Morse Code Telegraph

Two Arduino terminals exchange Morse code over a wired serial link, with LCD histories, indicator LEDs, and audible feedback. Became part of the Microcontrollers Workshop in Farmingdale's IEEE Student Branch club.

Platform
Arduino Uno R3
Components
Pushbuttons, LEDs, piezo buzzers, 16×2 LCDs, potentiometers, resistors, jumper wires
  • Read the lab manual (PDF)

Overview

A pair of Arduino-based telegraph terminals lets two people send and receive Morse code. Each terminal has a pushbutton key, transmit and receive LEDs, a piezo buzzer, and a 16×2 LCD. The display keeps separate histories of outgoing and incoming dots and dashes.

The accompanying lab manual includes parts lists, wiring diagrams, the Arduino sketch, testing steps, and a Morse code guide.

In Fall 2026, I designed this concept to be a project in Farmingdale's IEEE club Microcontroller workshop.

Video demonstration

Hardware and display

The physical build uses a serial connection between the two Uno boards. Each LCD records transmitted Morse on its top row and received Morse on its bottom row. The indicators and buzzers provide feedback while a key is held.

Tinkercad circuit

The simulation shows the two terminals and their connections. The lab manual distinguishes the simulated serial wiring from the physical build: the simulation uses D0/D1, while the physical version uses D8/D9 with AltSoftSerial.
